S01.title: Learn about rent increases in San Francisco
S01.verifies: 1.6% current rate; license requirement; 12-month/anniversary rule; 30/90-day notice; +5 days if mailed; rate in effect on effective date; base rent only; no rounding up; no extra rent for additional occupants; worked examples

S02.title: Current Rates, including Rent Increase, Relocation, Sec. Deposit
S02.verifies: Allowable rent increase 1.6% (3/1/26-2/28/27), 1.4% (3/1/25-2/28/26), 1.7% (3/1/24-2/28/25); security deposit interest; bankable Rent Board fees; link to Form 571

S03.title: Form 571: Allowable Annual Rent Increases (1982-present), 26-27 edition
S03.verifies: Full official historical table of allowable annual increases; 'may increase the tenant's base rent once every 12 months ... without filing a petition at the Rent Board'

S05.title: The Rent Board Housing Inventory
S05.verifies: All owners must report; license automatically generated for non-owner-occupied units after reporting; March 1 annual deadline; license must be on file before an increase can go into effect; license does NOT need to be included with the rent increase notice; reporting deadlines by building size; bulk upload 5+ units; what must be reported

S06.title: Notice of Owner Noncompliance with Housing Inventory
S06.verifies: 'A current Rent Increase License must be on file with the San Francisco Rent Board before any annual or banked rent increase goes into effect'; unlicensed increase may be null and void; tenant petition routes; how to check license status in the Portal

S07.title: Sec. 37.15 - Reporting Obligations; Licensing (Rent Ordinance text)
S07.verifies: Statutory text: owners report under penalty of perjury; 7/1/2022 for 10+ unit buildings; 3/1/2023 for condos and <10-unit buildings; license issued on substantial compliance; license suspended during noncompliance; tenant not obligated to pay increased rent for months during suspension

S08.title: Rent Board Rules and Regulations, Part XIII, Section 13.14 Licensing
S08.verifies: 'Any rent increase ... purporting to be effective while the landlord is unlicensed shall render the entire rent increase null and void'; the EFFECTIVE DATE, not the date of service, controls; banking rights preserved; applies to increases effective on/after 7/1/2022 (3/1/2023 for condos and <10-unit buildings)

S09.title: New Legislation Creates A Housing Inventory And Requires Owners To Obtain a License (Ord. 265-20)
S09.verifies: Ordinance No. 265-20 effective 1/18/2021; list of required reported information; phase-in dates; 'license will only be issued ... if the owner is in substantial compliance'; suspension for noncompliance

S10.title: Banked rent increases
S10.verifies: Banking rules; no limit; no expiry during tenancy; do not carry over to a new tenant; banked increases need no Rent Board approval but must be calculated correctly, not compounded or prorated; notice must state which part is banked; states a 24-full-month rule (CONFLICT - see Flagged for Review)

S11.title: Annual rent increase for multiple years
S11.verifies: Add up allowable increases for skipped years; no petition required; no compounding; no rounding up; 30-day written notice (35 if mailed); base rent only

S12.title: Increasing rents during irregular periods
S12.verifies: Anniversary date = date of last increase, or lease start date if never increased; 12-24 month and 24+ month scenarios; one increase per 12 months; no compounding; 30-day notice (35 if mailed); risk of losing an increase when the effective date is moved

S13.title: Sec. 37.3 - Rent Limitations (Rent Ordinance text)
S13.verifies: 37.3(a)(1) annual increase, 7% ceiling, license; (a)(2) banking; (a)(8) petition for additional increases; (a)(11) no increase solely for additional occupant; (b) notice content, (b)(5) nonconforming increases null and void; (d)(1)(A)(ii) rent control continues for a new tenancy after a 1946.1/827 notice; (d)(2)(B) no market reset on partial change in occupancy; (f) Costa-Hawkins vacancy control

S14.title: Sec. 37.2 - Definitions (Rent Ordinance text)
S14.verifies: 'Base Rent' = rent charged on initial occupancy plus allowable imposed increases, excluding 37.7 capital improvement increases and passthroughs; (h) 'Landlord' = an owner, lessor, sublessor ... and the agent, representative or successor - no corporate carve-out

S15.title: Rent Board Rules & Regulations, Part IV (Sections 4.10, 4.12)
S15.verifies: 4.10(a) notice must break out annual/banked/capital/utility/RAP portions; 4.10(b) nonconforming increases null and void (good-faith 0.5% tolerance); 4.12(a) banking: one increase per 12 months, only increases available on/after 4/1/1982, 'A full 12 months must have elapsed', no compounding, no rounding up; 4.12(b) notice must state banked portion and dates

S16.title: Rent Board Rules & Regulations, Part VI (Sections 6.10, 6.12, 6.13, 6.14)
S16.verifies: 6.10 O&M expense justification requires actual costs and proof of payment; 6.12 unfilled repair requests can defeat an increase; 6.13 no extra rent for additional occupants; 6.14 unlimited increase only when all original occupants no longer reside and a timely written 6.14 notice was served

S17.title: Landlord Petitions and Passthroughs
S17.verifies: Six types of increases that require a landlord petition BEFORE serving the notice; supporting documentation required; no filing charge; tenants need not pay until approved; petitions for 6.14/Costa-Hawkins determination are optional; bond/utility worksheets must be filed first

S18.title: Learn about San Francisco rental laws
S18.verifies: Units built on or before June 13, 1979 and not used as a single-family dwelling 'may have both' rent control and eviction protection; exemptions; Property Information Map for build date; free Rent Board counseling

S19.title: Roommates and subletting
S19.verifies: 'Landlords in San Francisco cannot charge more rent simply because a new roommate ... has moved into a unit. This is illegal, no matter what the lease itself says'; any agreement to pay more is void and unenforceable; tenant petition available

S20.title: Rent Increases Under Section 6.14 And Costa-Hawkins
S20.verifies: Market-rate increase only when the LAST original occupant vacates; 6.14 notice within a reasonable time (generally 60 days); co-tenants are not subject to such an increase; no petition required but tenant may challenge

S21.title: The Rent Board Fee
S21.verifies: 2026-2027 fee $59.00 per dwelling unit / $29.50 guest unit; 50% recoverable from tenants in occupancy ($29.50 / $14.75); March 1 deadline; late penalties

S22.title: Report an unlawful rent increase or request a review of your rent history
S22.verifies: Tenant petition alleging unlawful rent increase: no charge, NO TIME LIMIT for filing; hearing before an Administrative Law Judge; evidence, cross-examination, written decision, appeal

S23.title: Tenant Summary Petitions
S23.verifies: Tenant may file when a rent increase notice is clearly unlawful on its face; usually no hearing; landlord then serves a corrected notice; new effective date sets a new anniversary date

S24.title: Tenant and Landlord Resources (MOHCD)
S24.agency: City & County of San Francisco / sf.gov
S24.verifies: Free legal help from Eviction Defense Collaborative; tenant counseling organizations for rent increase notices; landlord resources; Bay Area Legal Aid small claims clinic

S25.title: Rent Board Referral Listing
S25.verifies: Official listing of tenant advocacy and free/low-cost legal resources (SF Tenants Union, Housing Rights Committee, Bay Area Legal Aid, Legal Assistance to the Elderly, Open Door Legal Sunset office in 94122, etc.); 'You do not need a lawyer to file a petition at the Rent Board'

S26.title: Speak with a Rent Board counselor
S26.verifies: Free phone/in-person counseling for tenants AND landlords; 'We cannot give legal advice'; 415-252-4600; multilingual

S27.title: The California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
S27.verifies: 8.8% maximum for AB 1482 units in SF (8/1/2026-7/31/2027), 'This does NOT apply for units under the rent increase limitations of the San Francisco Rent Ordinance'; units already subject to a more restrictive local ordinance are exempt from the state cap; corporate-ownership condition for the SFH/condo exemption

S28.title: About Rent Board (services and limits)
S28.verifies: Rent Ordinance enacted 6/13/1979; 'Cases of discrimination or retaliation (contact the San Francisco Human Rights Commission for these issues)'; free counseling; mediations

S29.title: Human Rights Commission
S29.agency: City & County of San Francisco / sf.gov
S29.verifies: Housing discrimination is illegal in San Francisco; Civil Rights Division investigates and mediates discrimination complaints in housing

S30.title: California Civil Code Section 827
S30.verifies: 30-day written notice for increases of 10% or less; 90-day written notice if the increase alone or combined with another increase in the preceding 12 months exceeds 10%; service by mail subject to Code of Civil Procedure 1013

S31.title: California Civil Code Section 1947.12 (Tenant Protection Act)
S31.verifies: 5% + CPI or 10% whichever is lower; (d)(3) EXEMPTS housing subject to a local rent control ordinance that restricts annual increases to less than 5% + CPI; (d)(5)(A) SFH/condo exemption unavailable to a REIT, a corporation, or an LLC with a corporate member; (e) notice per 827

S32.title: California Civil Code Section 1954.53 (Costa-Hawkins)
S32.verifies: Owner may establish initial rental rate except where the previous tenancy was terminated by a 1946.1 notice or a change in terms noticed under 827, and other exceptions

S33.title: California Government Code Section 12955 (FEHA housing discrimination)
S33.verifies: Unlawful for an owner of housing to discriminate against or harass any person because of race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information; (f) retaliation prohibited

S34.title: Housing Discrimination Under the Fair Housing Act
S34.verifies: Housing discrimination is illegal in nearly all housing including private housing; protected classes: race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status, disability; HUD complaint route

S35.title: 42 U.S.C. Section 3604 (Fair Housing Act statutory text)
S35.verifies: Sec. 804(b): 'To discriminate against any person in the terms, conditions, or privileges of sale or rental of a dwelling ... because of race, color, religion, sex, familial status, or national origin' is unlawful; (f)(2) disability

S36.title: San Francisco Property Information Map
S36.verifies: Official tool the Rent Board directs owners to use to check when a building was built (rent-control coverage check)

S37.title: Rent Board Portal
S37.verifies: Official portal for Housing Inventory reporting, Rent Board fee payment, and public lookup of Rent Increase License status

S38.title: The Rent Ordinance (Chapter 37 index)
S38.verifies: Index of Chapter 37 sections including 37.15; includes the Rent Board's disclaimer that its version 'is not the official record of the laws or regulations of the City and County of San Francisco'

S39.title: Form 516C: Tenant Petition for Unlawful Rent Increase
S39.verifies: Official tenant petition form; Costa-Hawkins/6.14 grounds include 'An original occupant still permanently resides in the unit'

S40.title: Rent Board Forms Center (Form 518 Tenant Summary Petition; Form 516C Unlawful Rent Increase)
S40.verifies: Official Rent Board Forms Center: Form 518 Tenant Summary Petition is 'for tenants who have received a rent increase notice that is clearly unlawful on its face and has not yet gone into effect'; Form 516C is the Unlawful Rent Increase petition

S41.title: Housing Trust Fund Five-Year Report 2019-2023 (Tenant Right to Counsel)
S41.verifies: 'In June 2018, San Francisco voters passed the No Eviction Without Representation Act to establish the Tenant Right to Counsel program, which provides free legal assistance for residents facing eviction'

S42.title: Memo re Proposed Changes to Rules & Regulations 1.12 (Jan 2, 2026)
S42.verifies: Documents that October 2025 CPI data was not published by the U.S. Department of Labor and that the Rent Board considered temporary alternate CPI methodologies for the 3/1/2026 and 3/1/2027 rates

S43.title: Form 538: 2024-25 Bond Measure Worksheet (license note)
S43.verifies: Form states the 37.15 license requirement applies to increases effective on/after 7/1/2020 (10+ units) and 3/1/2021 (condos, <10 units) - CONFLICTS with Rules 13.14 / sf.gov; flagged for review

S44.title: Notice to Tenant required by 37.9(c) (Tenant Right to Counsel text)
S44.verifies: Official City notice: 'You are eligible for free assistance through the Tenant Right to Counsel Program' with Eviction Defense Collaborative intake contact

S45.title: Rent Board home page (current 1.6% calculator)
S45.verifies: 'This year's allowed rent increase is 1.6%' for 3/1/2026-2/28/2027; portal and Housing Inventory links

S46.title: Minutes of the Rent Board, January 13, 2026
S46.verifies: Official minutes of the January 13, 2026 regular Rent Board meeting; the Commissioners' communications list includes 'Notice of Public Hearing Scheduled for January 13, 2026' and 'Rent Board Updated Memorandum Regarding Proposed Changes to Rules and Regulations Section 1.12 dated January 2, 2026'

S47.title: HUD Handbook 4350.1 REV-1, Chapter 7: Processing Budgeted Rent Increases and Fees for Certain HUD Projects
S47.verifies: Paragraph 7-21: 'Owners are allowed to charge only the rents shown on the rent schedule they submitted and which have most recently been authorized by HUD.' Chapter 7 applies only to the listed HUD-insured/subsidized projects; it is not a general federal rent cap

S48.title: San Francisco Analysis of Impediments to Fair Housing Choice (July 2020 - June 2025)
S48.agency: City & County of San Francisco / media.api.sf.gov

Its table of contents lists Section IV.A.10 'Other State/Local Protected Classes'; the section text was beyond the retrievable page range in this verification pass, so this project does NOT assert any specific additional local protected class from it

S49.title: Repository commit history (initial commit b747350)
S49.verifies: The project began with a single README.md and no pre-existing research, data, site, or coordination file

S51.title: Tenant Petitions (Rent Board)
S51.verifies: 'There is no charge for filing the petition'; lists unlawful rent increase and Tenant Summary Petition claims; states 'the Rent Board cannot decide matters that are not covered by the Rent Ordinance ... we do not adjudicate issues that are not related to the amount of rent charged, such as harassment, discrimination and retaliation'
